editorial:
Imagine hopping in a kayak and paddling across the planet to see the world's most famous rivers. That is exactly what Mark Angelo does in this eye-opening journey. You get to travel along with him as he explores beautiful waters, but the vibe quickly shifts from a nature trip to a mystery. As he moves from one country to another, you start to see something scary happening to the water. He discovers that the rivers are turning strange colors and becoming toxic, and he spends the movie digging into why this is happening to our planet.

What really hits home is how the film connects your own closet to the pollution in these rivers. The pacing is steady, and the footage of the colorful, dyed water is honestly shocking to see. While some parts feel a bit like a school lesson, the real-world footage makes it feel urgent. If you care about the earth, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV or stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture quality. Adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is also a great call if you want to show it to your family.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up by showing that the fashion industry is the main reason rivers are dying. You see the final evidence of chemicals from clothing dyes poisoning the water and the people living nearby. Mark ends his journey with a call to action, telling you that your shopping habits can help save these rivers. It finishes on a serious note, urging you to demand cleaner production from big brands to stop the pollution.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves nature and wants to learn about the planet.
